description: AI Factory health signal catalog. Each profile classifies one Azure resource type (optionally by kind or hierarchical namespace) and lists curated Azure Monitor platform-metric signals. Thresholds are defaults; override them per deployment with signal overrides.

layers.description: Foundry account and projects, model deployments, AI Search, Cosmos DB agent state, Bot Service and AI services.
Project storage accounts, data lakes and relational or cache databases.
Azure Machine Learning, AKS, Databricks and Data Factory.
Container Apps, App Service, Logic Apps, Event Hubs and API Management.
Key Vaults holding project secrets and keys.
Application Insights and Log Analytics. Limited impact: an observability problem degrades but never fails the workload.
Common resource group services that a project depends on (Log Analytics and the data lake).
Admin (DSVM) and build-agent virtual machines in the common resource group.
Nested project health models, one per AI Factory project.

nonResourceFlags.enableAMPLS: Azure Monitor Private Link Scope lives in the hub subscription and is telemetry network plumbing, not a project or common workload resource.
nonResourceFlags.enableAIFactoryHub: Configuration intent only; it deploys nothing.
nonResourceFlags.enablePublicGenAIAccess: Network access setting applied to the modelled AI services.
nonResourceFlags.enablePublicAccessWithPerimeter: Network perimeter setting applied to the modelled AI services.
nonResourceFlags.enableDeleteForDisabledResources: Pipeline lifecycle switch, not a resource.
nonResourceFlags.enableDefenderforAISubLevel: Microsoft Defender for Cloud plan setting, not a monitored resource.
nonResourceFlags.enableDefenderforAIResourceLevel: Microsoft Defender for Cloud plan setting, not a monitored resource.
nonResourceFlags.enableAISearchSharedPrivateLink: Networking option of the modelled AI Search service.
nonResourceFlags.enableRetries: Pipeline retry switch, not a resource.
nonResourceFlags.enableAppInsightsDashboard: Portal dashboard; it is not a runtime dependency of the workload.
nonResourceFlags.enableElasticsearch: Elastic Cloud (Microsoft.Elastic) is a partner SaaS without Azure Monitor platform metrics; monitor it in Elastic.
nonResourceFlags.ENABLE_KONG: Kong edge proxy is a container workload with no dedicated Azure resource type; its hosting platform and the modelled API Management carry its health.

notMonitorable.microsoft.containerregistry/registries: Verified on the test factory: Azure Resource Health returns HTTP 422 (not supported) for container registries, and the registry Transactions metric exposes no documented failure response types. Monitor image pulls through the consuming AKS, Azure ML and Container Apps entities; add a signal here once a failure dimension value is validated.
notMonitorable.microsoft.app/jobs: Verified on the test factory: Azure Resource Health returns HTTP 422 (not supported) for Container Apps jobs, and the Executions metric's 'state' values could not be confirmed (no executions in 30 days). Add a failed-execution signal here once a state value is validated.

profiles.description: Foundry (AIServices) account hosting model deployments. Availability is gated by request volume so a few failed calls in a quiet period do not page anyone.
Standalone Azure OpenAI account; same gated availability as Foundry.
Single-purpose AI services (Vision, Speech, Document Intelligence, Content Safety, Language, Translator).
Foundry project with the standard-agent capability host (Cosmos DB threads, AI Search vectors, project storage). Resource Health is not available for this child resource.

signals.name: thread-store-throttling
signals.displayName: Agent thread store (Cosmos DB) throttled requests (count)

profiles.description: Capability-host vector store and retrieval index.
Channel endpoint for Foundry agents (Teams, web chat). Resource Health is not used because Bot Service is a global resource.
Bing grounding / custom search account used by agents.
Project blob/file storage, including the capability-host file store. Client errors such as 404 are normal and are not treated as failures.
Storage account with hierarchical namespace: the AI Factory data lake.
AKS for Azure ML inference or standalone workloads.

Databricks workspaces emit no Azure Monitor platform metrics and Azure Resource Health is not supported for them (both verified on the test factory). Health comes from Databricks diagnostic logs in Log Analytics (opt-in with --log-signals).
profiles.noSourceHint: Azure Databricks workspaces emit no platform metrics and do not support Resource Health. Send the workspace's 'jobs' diagnostic logs (DatabricksJobs) to Log Analytics and redeploy with --log-signals to model them.

logAnalyticsSignals.name: failed-job-runs
logAnalyticsSignals.displayName: Failed Databricks job runs (count per hour)

profiles.description: Agent front ends, the private Azure MCP server and other project apps. Scale-to-zero apps simply report no data.
Workload telemetry: request, exception and dependency failures reported by the project's apps and agents.

Admin DSVM and self-hosted build agents. Resource Health is disabled by default because the DSVM auto-shutdown deallocates it nightly; a deallocated VM reports no availability data instead of failing.
A project health model nested in the factory (common) model. Its root entity state rolls up; it needs no signals.
